# libarchive 3.8.9 — pinned vendored build recipe (FloeAndroid, lane job-bf610b6f22fe42ab)

Purpose: the Android equivalent of the iOS signed `CArchive.xcframework`
produced by `FloeAgent/scripts/bootstrap_libarchive.py` at public baseline
3fd597b5 — the bounded read-only RAR decoder behind
`FloeWorkspace/RARArchiveService.swift`. Same upstream version and same
SHA-256 pin: 3.8.9 / f5a6539059cf5e597dbeda37bfa4874b1e8dea063c8d93bf85a2b44af90a5bd4.

## What is vendored
- `libarchive/` — exactly the 123 `.c` units `archive_static` compiles
  (verified identical list on Apple host arm64 and Android NDK arm64-v8a)
  plus all upstream `*.h`; CLI/windows/unused-ACL variants excluded.
- `floe/config.h` — platform selector; `floe/config-macos.h` and
  `floe/config-android.h` are the exact `config.h` files generated by the
  CMake invocations below, frozen.
- `floe/android_lf.h` — upstream `contrib/android/include/android_lf.h`
  (referenced by `archive.h` when building for Android; gives the file64
  large-file mapping on android-28).
- `COPYING` (BSD-2-clause), `SOURCE-PIN.json`.

## Reproduction (verified 2026-10-24 on this host)
```bash
# both configs share the iOS bootstrap's option set (everything OFF except
# ZLIB, static, Release), which fixes the format/filter refusal behavior.
FLAGS="-DENABLE_TEST=OFF -DENABLE_TAR=OFF -DENABLE_CPIO=OFF -DENABLE_CAT=OFF
  -DENABLE_UNZIP=OFF -DENABLE_OPENSSL=OFF -DENABLE_MBEDTLS=OFF
  -DENABLE_NETTLE=OFF -DENABLE_LIBB2=OFF -DENABLE_LZMA=OFF -DENABLE_LZO=OFF
  -DENABLE_LZ4=OFF -DENABLE_ZSTD=OFF -DENABLE_BZip2=OFF -DENABLE_LIBXML2=OFF
  -DENABLE_EXPAT=OFF -DENABLE_PCREPOSIX=OFF -DENABLE_PCRE2POSIX=OFF
  -DENABLE_ICONV=OFF -DENABLE_ACL=OFF -DENABLE_XATTR=OFF -DENABLE_ZLIB=ON
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF
  -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON -DENABLE_WERROR=OFF"

# 1. Apple host (test builds)
cmake -S libarchive-3.8.9 -B build-macos $FLAGS
cmake --build build-macos --target archive_static

# 2. Android production (NDK r30, arm64-v8a, android-28, flexible 16 KiB)
cmake -S libarchive-3.8.9 -B build-android \
  -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE="$NDK/build/cmake/android.toolchain.cmake" \
  -DANDROID_ABI=arm64-v8a -DANDROID_PLATFORM=android-28 \
  -DANDROID_SUPPORT_FLEXIBLE_PAGE_SIZES=ON $FLAGS
cmake --build build-android --target archive_static
```
`floe/verify-compile.sh` recompiles all 123 units on both platforms against
the vendored tree and the frozen config (proves the SwiftPM definition set
below is self-sufficient; objects are not linked here — 16 KiB alignment is
a final-`.so` link property, see the xz RECIPE note).

## SwiftPM target proposal (Main applies to shared/Package.swift)
```swift
.target(
    name: "CArchive", // keeps the upstream import name used by the decoder service
    path: "Vendor/Archive/libarchive-3.8.9",
    sources: /* the 123 relative libarchive/*.c paths in SOURCE-PIN order */,
    publicHeadersPath: "libarchive",
    cSettings: [
        .define("HAVE_CONFIG_H"),
        .define("LIBARCHIVE_STATIC"),
        .define("__LIBARCHIVE_ENABLE_VISIBILITY"),
        .define("NDEBUG"),
        .headerSearchPath("libarchive"),
        .headerSearchPath("floe"),   // config.h + android_lf.h
    ],
    linkerSettings: [.linkedLibrary("z")]
)
```
No Package.resolved entry (path-vendored source, like the ZIPFoundation/CZLib
mirror precedent). `FloeWorkspace` gains the `CArchive` dependency; the
product `.so` links it transitively.

## Semantics notes (honest deltas vs iOS)
- iOS links a prebuilt *signed* XCFramework (App Store signing of the
  binary). On Android the framework signing concept does not apply: the
  decoder is compiled from these exact pinned sources in Main's reproducible
  graph, and the shipped `.so` carries the app signature. The Swift refusal
  contract is unchanged either way.
- Same option set ⇒ same refusal behavior for encrypted/multipart/unsupported
  archives (`archive_read_*` failures surface through the service's `checked`
  mapping). PPMd-capable RAR3 files decode via upstream's bundled ppmd7/ppmd8
  objects (included in the 123-unit set); zlib is the system library on both
  platforms (NDK public `libz`, macOS host `libz`).

## Overlay additions (documented, this lane)
`libarchive/module.modulemap` + `libarchive/CArchive.h` — the same
two-header umbrella (`archive.h` + `archive_entry.h`) the iOS
`bootstrap_libarchive.py` generates, so clang never scans the internal
`archive_*_private.h` headers as module units. No upstream file modified.
